Looking at the cuboid (3×3×2 = 18 cubes = three pieces of 6 cubes):

- **Visible dark cubes:** the full column of three at the front right, plus one cube behind the bottom cube of that column (seen on the right face) — 4 cubes.
- **Hidden cubes:** the only cubes not visible from front/top/right are the four interior back cubes. The white piece must use the hidden cube touching its visible back cube, leaving the dark piece able to take only the two hidden cubes that keep it connected: the two back-bottom cubes extending left from the visible back cube.

So the dark piece consists of a vertical rod of 3 cubes (front right column) joined end-to-end, at right angles, with a horizontal rod of 3 cubes running along the back bottom edge.

Checking the options: this is exactly shape **C** — a vertical column of three with a row of three attached perpendicularly at its base (drawn shifted up because it lies in the back layer). The other shapes either have wrong branching (C-shaped/T-shaped junctions), are flat (A, B, D), or place the extra cube in a position that doesn't fit (E).

\boxed{C}
